source.title: Representations Have Trajectories: Characterizing Temporal Representation Dynamics in Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is supplied. Some table/figure layout is flattened, but the extracted results below have explicit text or recoverable table entries.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether training outcomes vary with architecture, depth, initialization and residual connections, and reports CIFAR-10 training outcomes. Its main measures are representation rank and loss, rather than the versions’ core training-error measure.
record.gate_note: The study measures rank dynamics and optimization outcomes during training. It reports CIFAR-10 training loss and accuracy, but does not report training classification error as zero or near-zero; it does not test the versions’ claims about training error on CIFAR-10/100, label corruption, two-layer ReLU spurious minima, or learning rates above the stability limit. Synthetic regression uses teacher-student data, not classification benchmarks.
record.test_reason: The study measures representation trajectories and associated optimization outcomes. It does not establish near-zero CNN training classification error, a CNN depth-degradation contrast rescued by identity shortcuts, initialization effects on training speed or trainable depth, or a batch-normalization speed or learning-rate advantage. The explicit depth-by-shortcut training-accuracy comparison concerns ViTs, outside V3's stated CNN scope.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. Recovery trajectories are associated with convergence, persistent DRC usually accompanies failure, and residual connections accompany fewer DRC cases and delayed rank decay. Early trajectory categories also forecast eventual outcomes descriptively. These are configuration-dependent associations, not demonstrated causal effects; DRC is generally present by the first logged epoch, and some DRC regression runs still reach low absolute loss.
record.recipe_differences: Studies temporal representation rank and regression/classification optimization outcomes; it does not reproduce the original studies' interventions or training-error measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Trajectory prevalence and optimization outcomes vary with architecture, depth, optimizer, activation, initialization and residual type. In CIFAR-10, no-residual ViTs show depth-wise rank contraction; batch-normalized plain CNNs with depth-32 SIREN and SGD can have vanished gradients.

fits_no_version.finding: Without residuals, ViT mean training accuracy declines from 74.3% to 66.6% to 52.8% at depths 3, 6 and 9; residual counterparts achieve 87.0%, 83.2% and 91.9%. Depth-9 DRC occurs in 2/8 no-residual runs and 0/8 residual runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested CIFAR-10 ViTs, removing residual connections accompanies worsening training accuracy with depth; residual configurations avoid this monotonic decline.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the balanced three-seed synthetic grid, DRC occurs in 996/3402 default-initialized runs and 1850/3402 rank-one-initialized runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization changes the incidence of persistent representation collapse in these synthetic regression networks.

fits_no_version.finding: All 18 high-rank depth-32 SIREN CNNs under SGD fail to optimize, with mean training loss 2.6550 and reported zero layerwise gradients; all 41 DRC CNNs have chance-level test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation rank alone does not diagnose optimization success; persistent rank-one collapse and vanished gradients identify distinct failure configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: The six ResNet runs retain effective rank 11.58–14.45, and Section 8.1 describes low training and test loss across the residual-architecture sweeps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested ResNet configurations preserve substantial effective rank and are described as optimizing successfully, including configurations with skips disabled.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic collapse-and-recovery trajectories reach loss below 0.001 in 82.89% of runs versus 26.97% for other trajectories; a low-stable-rank CNN with substantial effective rank reaches 90.35% test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recovery trajectories are associated with synthetic optimization success, while low stable rank alone can coexist with successful classification.

record.problems: The CIFAR-10 outcomes are reported as training/test loss or accuracy rather than training classification error. Several architecture comparisons are aggregate and not matched for all training conditions. The authors note that the DRC threshold was selected using the same CIFAR-10 sweep, so its accuracy consistency check is not independent validation. The ViT early-stuck group is small (n=2).
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted; results without the claim's classification-error measure are included only where they test architecture, initialization, or normalization-related versions via reported optimization outcomes. Synthetic association statistics and the single benign low-stable-rank CNN case are summarized in fits_no_version rather than mapped to the listed versions.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large randomly initialized CNNs; CIFAR-100 and corrupted or random labels; size, early-stopping and regularization qualifications.
Spurious-local-minimum frequencies in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and their reduction with one or two extra student neurons.

Higher training error with increasing depth in plain batch-normalized CNNs, its persistence under longer training, and prevention by matched identity shortcuts; the special tanh initialization and Fixup provisions.

Activation-matched signal and gradient preservation as a determinant of training speed and trainable depth; matched-variance orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh training; orthogonal convolution kernels at extreme depth.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, divergence boundaries and edge-of-stability training.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, and equivalent speed and stability with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the extracted limits_scope verdicts: an untested component or a result on a different construct does not limit a version. Accuracy can be converted directly to classification error; test accuracy, representation rank and unspecified low training loss cannot establish near-zero training classification error.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports CIFAR-10 training loss and accuracy, but not training classification error. It does not report CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, comparisons with smaller models or early stopping, or the cited Zhang/Nakkiran recipes.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student classification or spurious-local-minimum frequency sweep by teacher/student width is tested.

Tests CIFAR-10 plain CNNs and residual architectures in relation to rank dynamics and optimization outcomes, but does not compare plain batch-normalized networks with the same networks with identity shortcuts using training classification error, or report ImageNet results. It does not test the cited special initialization or Fixup recipes.

Compares default and low-rank initialization in synthetic regression for rank-trajectory categories; does not test activation-matched initializations, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, tanh training speed, or 10,000-layer plain CNN training.
No above-stability learning-rate, curvature, sharpness, catapult, or edge-of-stability experiment.

Plain CNNs use batch normalization, and residual architectures are evaluated, but the paper does not compare training speed or learning-rate tolerance with and without batch normalization, nor test Fixup.

rows.subject: Plain CNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained plain CNN configurations and summarized high-rank Archetype 1 outcomes.

conditions.value: 18/192; all depth 32 SIREN CNNs under SGD

rows.note: Reports training loss but no training classification error value or threshold. All 18 models failed to optimize, with layerwise gradients reported as vanished.
rows.check: The training loss of 2.6550 and stated optimization failure are correctly extracted. They do not establish training classification error or whether these configurations meet V1's sufficient-size conditions. Separate default from deliberately low-rank initialization before interpreting spontaneous failures.

rows.subject: Plain CNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained plain CNN configurations and summarized DRC outcomes.
rows.measure: Test accuracy and test cross-entropy, alongside training outcome description
rows.value: All 41 at chance accuracy; mean test cross-entropy 2.4445. Text says all 41 are at chance accuracy with test cross-entropy near baseline.
rows.locator: Section 8.2; Appendix C, Table S.7 and Fig. S.6
rows.note: The paper reports test accuracy and test loss for DRC models and says they fail, but does not report their training classification error.
rows.check: Test accuracy and test loss do not measure V1's training classification error. The cited Table S.7 and Figure S.6 describe a benign low-rank example; Section 8.2 and Figure S.7 support the DRC comparison. The mean test loss is 2.4445, rather than exactly the theoretical baseline of 2.3026.

rows.subject: ResNet-18/50
rows.operation_detail: Trained residual architectures and reported final rank and qualitative training/test loss outcomes.
rows.measure: Training and test loss; end-of-training effective rank
rows.value: Residual architectures reached low training and test loss; 6 ResNet runs retain end effective rank 11.58–14.45.
rows.note: The statement is aggregate across residual architectures; no specific loss values, training error rate, or batch-normalization comparison is given.
rows.check: Qualitative low loss and effective rank do not establish V1's near-zero training error or V6's normalization advantage. The six runs include skip-Off configurations, so they cannot collectively demonstrate an identity-shortcut benefit under V3. Table S.28 supplies configurations, not numerical loss results.

rows.subject: Plain CNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained batch-normalized plain CNNs and related training outcomes to rank trajectory and gradient behavior.
rows.measure: Training loss and layerwise gradient norms
rows.value: All 18 failed to optimize; mean training loss = 2.6550; layerwise gradient norms vanished to 0.000000 for every layer.
rows.note: Shows a failure mode in deep plain CNNs, but does not compare depth-specific training classification error or test an identity-shortcut counterpart under the same recipe.
rows.check: Duplicates R1's failed-run group with gradient diagnostics. No matched shallower or identity-shortcut CNN training-error comparison establishes V3, and no normalization ablation establishes V6.

rows.subject: ResNet-18/50
rows.operation_detail: Trained residual architectures with skip modes and summarized their rank and loss outcomes.
rows.measure: Training and test loss; end-of-training effective rank
rows.value: Residual architectures reached low training and test loss and did not enter DRC; end effective rank 11.58–14.45.
rows.note: Supports successful optimization for the reported residual runs, but only qualitatively for loss and without a matched plain-network training-error comparison or normalization ablation.
rows.check: Duplicates R3. Successful optimization aggregated across skip-On, skip-Off and scaled configurations does not measure a shortcut advantage, and normalization is not ablated. The partial state is unsupported for either assigned version.

rows.subject: Synthetic models
rows.size_stated: 6,804 runs across three seeds; same 2,268 configurations per seed
rows.operation_detail: Compared default PyTorch Kaiming-uniform initialization with low-rank rank-one initialization for trajectory categories.
rows.note: Initialization changes DRC frequency, but this is a regression rank outcome, not a result on the initialization and trainability measures named in V4.
rows.check: The 29.3% DRC rate is correctly extracted, but representation-collapse incidence does not measure V4's learning speed or trainable depth under signal-preserving initialization.

rows.subject: Synthetic models
rows.size_stated: 6,804 runs across three seeds; same 2,268 configurations per seed
rows.operation_detail: Compared low-rank rank-one initialization with default PyTorch Kaiming-uniform initialization.
rows.note: Comparator condition for R6; measures DRC incidence in regression rather than the V4 claims about matched activation initialization and trainable depth.
rows.check: The 54.4% DRC rate is correctly extracted. This deliberately rank-one initialization comparison measures representation collapse, rather than V4's specified training outcomes.

rows.subject: Vision Transformer (ViT)
rows.operation_detail: Compared standard residual and no-residual ViTs across depths.
rows.measure: Training accuracy, test accuracy, and DRC incidence
rows.baseline: Standard residual ViT depth 9: training accuracy 91.9 ± 8.6%, test accuracy 77.2 ± 3.6%, DRC 0/8
rows.value: No-Residual ViT depth 9: training accuracy 52.8 ± 27.0%, test accuracy 49.2 ± 24.6%, DRC 2/8
rows.note: A different architecture family from V3's stated CNN comparison; no-residual depth-9 ViTs show lower accuracy and some DRC. The table reports mean accuracy, not training classification error.
rows.check: The numerical comparison is correctly extracted, but ViTs are outside V3's CNN scope. Training accuracy does measure classification error through its complement: depth-9 errors are 47.2% without residuals and 8.1% with residuals. The issue is architecture scope, not the use of accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
